groundwater = water stored under the ground in soil and rock
aquifer = an underground layer of rock that holds water
fertile soil = soil that is rich in nutrients and good for growing crops
soil erosion = the wearing away of topsoil by wind or water
weathering = the slow breaking down of rock by weather, water or plants
coral reef = an underwater structure built by corals, rich in marine life
mangrove forest = trees that grow in salty coastal water and protect the shore
tundra = a cold, treeless region with a short growing season
savannah = a grassy plain with scattered trees in a hot climate
woodland = land covered with trees, often smaller than a forest
forest canopy = the upper layer of leaves and branches in a forest
undergrowth = bushes and plants growing beneath the trees
peninsula = a piece of land almost surrounded by water
archipelago = a group of islands
plateau = a large area of high, fairly flat land
terrain = the physical features of an area of land
endangered species = a type of animal or plant at serious risk of dying out
habitat = the natural environment where a plant or animal lives
predator = an animal that hunts and kills other animals for food
prey = an animal that is hunted by another animal
